author: Athanasius of Alexandria
addressee: Eusebius, Lucifer, Asterius, Cymatius, and Anatolius, fellow ministers in Antioch
occasion: Athanasius and bishops with him in Alexandria write to leaders in Antioch to guide the reconciliation of groups divided by the Arian controversy and by disputes over theological language.
argument: The letter urges the Antiochene leaders to receive those who wish to make peace, requiring only that they anathematize the Arian heresy, confess the faith of Nicaea, and reject the view that the Holy Spirit is a creature. It reports that those who spoke of three hypostases and those who spoke of one hypostasis were examined and found to hold the same orthodox faith, differing only in terminology. It also records agreement on the incarnation: the Word himself became flesh, taking a complete human nature with soul and body. The letter forbids reading or producing the rumored Sardican document as a formula about faith, noting that the Council of Sardica itself decreed nothing further about faith and was satisfied with Nicaea, and urges an end to quarrels over words.

outline.move: Greeting and opening appeal for peace and unity, with instructions to receive returning groups on the basis of Nicaea and rejection of Arianism.
Condemnation of Arian and other heresies, and report of the examination of those who spoke of three hypostases.
Report of the examination of those who spoke of one hypostasis, and the agreement of both sides on the faith of Nicaea and on the incarnation.
Practical instructions to accept those who interpret their terms rightly, reject those who will not, and stop quarrels over words.
Subscriptions by Eusebius, Asterius, Paulinus, and Carterius, confirming the agreed interpretation and anathemas.

cast.name: Athanasius
cast.who: Archbishop of Alexandria and principal author of the letter.

cast.name: Eusebius
cast.who: Bishop of Vercelli in Gaul, one of the addressees and co-signer.

cast.name: Lucifer
cast.who: Bishop of the island of Sardinia, one of the addressees.

cast.name: Asterius
cast.who: Bishop of Petra in Arabia, one of the addressees and co-signer.

cast.name: Cymatius
cast.who: Bishop of Paltus in Coele Syria, one of the addressees.

cast.name: Anatolius
cast.who: Bishop of Euboea, one of the addressees.

cast.name: Paulinus
cast.who: Leader of one of the reconciling groups in Antioch, later a signatory.

cast.name: Carterius
cast.who: Signatory who adds a personal confession and anathemas; his title or see is not identified in the source.

voices.speaker: Athanasius and the bishops with him
voices.how_marked: The main body of the letter is written in their collective voice.

voices.speaker: Those who spoke of three hypostases
voices.how_marked: Their answers are reported in direct quotation introduced by 'they answered' (ἀπεκρίναντο), while the preceding examination is narrated.

voices.speaker: Those who spoke of one hypostasis
voices.how_marked: Their answers are reported in direct quotation introduced by 'they affirmed' (διεβεβαιώσαντο), with the voice shifting to first-person direct speech ('we say', 'we think').

voices.speaker: Eusebius
voices.how_marked: His subscription is introduced as translated from Latin.

voices.speaker: Asterius
voices.how_marked: His subscription is introduced by 'I, Asterius'.

voices.speaker: Paulinus
voices.how_marked: His subscription is introduced by 'I, Paulinus'.

voices.speaker: Carterius
voices.how_marked: His subscription is introduced by 'I, Carterius'.

key_terms.sense: The Son is of the same being or substance as the Father, as confessed at Nicaea.
A disputed term used by some for the three in the Trinity and by others as equivalent to 'being'; the letter shows both uses can be orthodox.
The being or substance of God, which the Son shares with the Father.
A created thing; the letter rejects calling the Holy Spirit or any member of the Trinity a creature.
Followers of Arius, used as a polemical name for those who deny the Son's full divinity.
The saving plan of God, especially the incarnation of the Savior in the flesh.
Flesh, used of the Word becoming human in the incarnation.
The confession of faith, especially the creed of Nicaea.
To condemn or curse a heresy or false teaching.
The Old Church, a meeting place or community in Antioch associated with one of the reconciling groups.
A document allegedly produced at the Council of Sardica, which the letter says should not be used.

scripture: The author cites the Septuagint and uses its book names and Psalm numbering. Modern citations should follow standard English Bible book names and Hebrew Psalm numbering where they differ from the Septuagint.
uncertain: The exact identity of the 'Old Church' community in Antioch beyond its association with one of the reconciling groups.
Whether the Sardican document mentioned was an actual written formula or only a rumored one.
The title or see of Carterius, who is not identified in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Lucifer: Bishop of the island of Sardinia
_unresolved_facts.fix: Bishop of the island of Sardis (Σαρδίας), not Sardinia

_unresolved_facts.claim: Those who spoke of one hypostasis: 'Their answers are reported in direct quotation introduced by 'they affirmed' (διεβεβαιώσαντο), with the voice shifting to first-person direct speech ('we say', 'we think').'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οἱ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ διεβεβαιώσαντο μήτε τοῦτο λέγειν, μήτε οὕτω πεφρονηκέναι πώποτε· ἀλλ' ὑπόστασιν μὲν λέγομεν, ἡγούμενοι ταὐτὸν εἶναι εἰπεῖν ὑπόστασιν καὶ οὐσίαν· μίαν δὲ φρονοῦμεν...
_unresolved_facts.fix: Their answers are reported with διεβεβαιώσαντο introducing indirect report, then shifting to first-person direct speech (λέγομεν, φρονοῦμεν, πιστεύομεν) without explicit quotation markers

_unresolved_facts.claim: Eusebius: 'His subscription is introduced as translated from Latin.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τούτοις καὶ Εὐσέβιος ὑπέγραψε Ῥωμαϊστί, ὧν ἡ ἑρμηνεία·
_unresolved_facts.fix: His subscription is noted as written 'in Latin' (Ῥωμαϊστί), with a Greek translation (ἑρμηνεία) following

_unresolved_facts.claim: The letter forbids reading or producing the rumored Sardican document as a formula about faith
_unresolved_facts.fix: The letter forbids reading or producing the Sardican document (πιττάκιον) at all (κωλύετε κἂν ὅλως ἀναγινώσκεσθαι ἢ προφέρεσθαι), not specifically 'as a formula about faith'—the document itself is rejected, not merely its use as a formula

_unresolved_facts.claim: noting that the Council of Sardica itself decreed nothing further about faith and was satisfied with Nicaea
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἡ δὲ ἁγία σύνοδος ἡ ἐν Σαρδικῇ συναχθεῖσα ἠγανάκτησε, καὶ ὥρισε μηδὲν ἔτι περὶ πίστεως γράφεσθαι, ἀλλ' ἀρκεῖσθαι τῇ ἐν Νικαίᾳ...
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Council of Sardica was angry (ἠγανάκτησε) at the attempt and decreed that nothing more should be written about faith, being satisfied with Nicaea—the emotional response and the decree against future writing are significant details
